parts.title: The History Of The Chicken
parts.article:
(A) Chicken as the universal food of our era, crossing cultural boundaries with ease. With its mild taste and uniform texture, chicken presents a blank canvas for the national flavours of almost any cuisine. However, until the introduction of large-scale industrial production in the 20th century, the economic and nutritional contribution of chickens was small. Chickens were considered as domestic birds that were useful to humanity, but unlike other animals such as the horse or the ox, they did little to change the course of history. Nonetheless, the chicken has inspired contributions to culture, art, cuisine, science and religion over the millennia. Chickens were, and still are, a sacred animal in some cultures. The hen is a worldwide symbol of nurturing and fertility. The rooster is a universal sign of masculinity.

(B) The domesticated chicken has a complicated family tree, stretching back 10,000 years. Recent DNA testing has shown that the chicken's wild ancestor is the red junglefowl. The bird's resemblance to modern chickens is seen in the red feathers on top of its head, the red flesh around its mouth, and its distinctive call in the morning. The females of this breed protect their eggs in the same way modern-day chickens do, and they make the same clucking sounds. In its habitat, which stretches from northeastern India to the Philippines, the red junglefowl looks on the forest floor for insects, seeds and fruit and flies up to nest in the trees at night. That's about as much flying as it can manage, a trait that made it relatively easy for humans to capture and domesticate it. But the red junglefowl is not the sole ancestor of the modern chicken. Scientists have identified three closely related species that might have bred with the red junglefowl. Precisely how much genetic material these other birds contributed to the DNA of domesticated chickens is unknown. However, recent research suggests that modern chickens inherited at least one trait, their yellow skin, from the grey junglefowl of southern India.

(C) Once chickens were domesticated, cultural contacts, trade, migration and territorial conquest resulted in their introduction to different regions around the world over several thousand years. Chickens arrived in Egypt in around 1750 BC, as fighting birds and additions to zoos. Drawings of the birds decorated royal tombs, which contained the treasures that the kings and queens would take to the afterlife. Yet it would be another 100 years before the bird became popular among ordinary Egyptians.

(D) It was in that era that Egyptians mastered the technique of artificial incubation, which freed hens to lay more eggs. This was not easy. Most chicken eggs will hatch in three weeks, but only if the temperature remains at around 38 degrees Celsius. The eggs must also be turned three to five times a day, and the humidity must remain stable at about 55 percent, otherwise physical deformities can result, or the eggs won't hatch. The Egyptians constructed vast complexes of large rooms, which were essentially ovens, and these were connected to a series of corridors and vents that allowed attendants to regulate the heat from fires. The egg attendants kept their methods a secret from outsiders for centuries.

(E) Around the Mediterranean, archaeologists have uncovered chicken bones from about 800 BC. Chickens were a delicacy among the Romans, whose culinary innovations included the omelette, and the practice of stuffing birds for cooking. European farmers began developing methods to fatten the birds, such as feeding them bread which had been soaked in wine. But the chicken's status in Europe appears to have diminished with the collapse of Rome. In the period after the fall of the Roman Empire, chicken farms vanished and the birds returned to the size they had been 1,000 years earlier.

(F) Well into the 20th century chickens, although valued as a source of eggs, played a relatively minor role in diet and the economy. Long after cattle had entered the industrial age of centralized and mechanized large-scale production, chicken production was still mostly a small-scale local enterprise. The breakthrough that made today's huge bird farms possible was the inclusion of antibiotics, along with a mixture of different vitamins, in the food chickens ate. This allowed chickens to be raised indoors and be protected from cold temperatures and heavy rain as well as predators. This factory farming represents the chicken's final step in its transformation into a big protein-producing business.

(G) Factory farms turning out an increasing amount of chicken have resulted in an increasing demand. Modern chickens are cogs in a system designed to convert grain into protein with staggering efficiency. It takes less than 1 kilogram of feed to produce 400 grams of chicken. By comparison, around 3 kilograms of feed are required to produce 400 grams of beef. A day-old chick can be turned into a 2 kilogram bird in six weeks - half the time it took two generations ago.

(H) Chickens also make wonderful pets, as breeders will tell you. They are as colourful as tropical fish but more affectionate, as cute as guinea pigs and better at catching mice than cats. In the USA, exotic and heritage breeds of chicken are being sold for considerable sums of money as the fashion for keeping chickens in the backyard becomes more popular.

(I) All in all, the globe-spanning chicken is an epic story of evolutionary, agricultural and culinary success, outnumbering human beings on the planet by nearly three to one.

Questions 1-7
Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 1?
In boxes 1-7 on your answer sheet, write:

Q1 Chicken is globally popular because it can be used for different styles of cooking.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q2 Chickens have poor capacity for flight compared to junglefowl.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q3 Scientists believe that the domestic chicken has more than one ancestor.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q4 A modern chicken has the same skin colour as the grey junglefowl.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q5 After the Roman Empire ended, chicken consumption in Europe declined.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q6 Some people criticise the methods involved in factory farming chickens.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q7 In the USA, fewer people are keeping expensive breeds of chicken at home.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

reference:
Q1

解析 鸡肉能跨越文化边界成为全球美食，是因为它味道清淡、肉质均匀，能像一张白纸一样完美融入几乎所有菜系的风味中。

干扰 你可能因为没看到直接表示因果的“because”就犹豫，但原文中“presents a blank canvas for...”正是对它为何能在全球流行的完美解释。

句子 Chicken as the universal food of our era, crossing cultural boundaries with ease. With its mild taste and uniform texture, chicken presents a blank canvas for the national flavours of almost any cuisine.

Q2

解析 文章只提到了红原鸡（junglefowl）的飞行能力十分有限，但完全没有将它的飞行能力与现代鸡进行比较，因此题目中的比较关系属于无中生有。

干扰 你可能会看到原文中提到了原鸡飞不高（只能飞到树上筑巢），就根据常识脑补现代鸡肯定飞得更差，但雅思阅读严禁自行推演，原文没有给出比较就是 NOT GIVEN。

句子 In its habitat, which stretches from northeastern India to the Philippines, the red junglefowl looks on the forest floor for insects, seeds and fruit and flies up to nest in the trees at night. That's about as much flying as it can manage, a trait that made it relatively easy for humans to capture and domesticate it.

Q3

解析 科学家确认红原鸡并非现代鸡唯一的祖先，还有其他三个近缘物种也参与了繁育。

干扰 你如果只看到段落开头说“野生祖先是红原鸡”就做判断很容易选错，接着往后看一句就会发现科学家指出它不止有一个祖先。

句子 But the red junglefowl is not the sole ancestor of the modern chicken. Scientists have identified three closely related species that might have bred with the red junglefowl

Q4

解析 现代鸡从印度南部的灰原鸡那里遗传了黄色的皮肤，说明它们的肤色是一样的。

干扰 你可能在找“the same”这个词，但既然皮肤颜色是直接“遗传（inherited）”过来的，那说明这两种鸡的肤色必然是相同的。

句子 However, recent research suggests that modern chickens inherited at least one trait, their yellow skin, from the grey junglefowl of southern India.

Q5

解析 罗马帝国衰落后，鸡在欧洲的地位大幅下降，养鸡场也随之消失，这说明人们对鸡肉的消费减少了。

干扰 你可能死盯原文找“消费（consumption）”这个词，但雅思阅读中“地位下降”和“养鸡场消失”就是消费下降最合理的同义替换。

句子 But the chicken's status in Europe appears to have diminished with the collapse of Rome. In the period after the fall of the Roman Empire, chicken farms vanished and the birds returned to the size they had been 1,000 years earlier.

Q6

解析 原文确实讲了工厂化养鸡把鸡变成了高效生产蛋白质的机器，但通篇完全没提到有任何人对这种工厂化方式提出过批评。

干扰 你可能凭常识觉得这种养鸡法很残忍肯定会被批评，但做题不能靠脑补，原文没写相关内容就必须选NOT GIVEN。

句子 This factory farming represents the chicken's final step in its transformation into a big protein-producing business. Factory farms turning out an increasing amount of chicken have resulted in an increasing demand. Modern chickens are cogs in a system designed to convert grain into protein with staggering efficiency.

Q7

解析 在美国，后院养鸡变得越来越流行，昂贵的鸡品种卖出了大价钱，说明养的人是变多了而不是变少了。

干扰 你可能光顾着看懂了“卖了大价钱”，却忽略了句末的“more popular”，把养鸡人数上升错当成了下降。

句子 In the USA, exotic and heritage breeds of chicken are being sold for considerable sums of money as the fashion for keeping chickens in the backyard becomes more popular.

Q8

解析 公元前1750年左右，鸡作为斗鸡和动物园（zoos）里的动物被引入了埃及。

干扰 你可能看到了前面的“fighting birds”，但别忘了填空缺的是“and”后面表示地点的名词“zoos”。

句子 Chickens arrived in Egypt in around 1750 BC, as fighting birds and additions to zoos.

Q9

解析 画着鸡的图案装饰在皇家陵墓（royal tombs）上，而这些陵墓里装有国王和王后的财宝。

干扰 你可能看到后面有财宝就想填“treasures”，但理顺句子主谓关系就知道，画作是用来装饰陵墓的，而不是画在财宝上的。

句子 Drawings of the birds decorated royal tombs, which contained the treasures that the kings and queens would take to the afterlife.

Q10

解析 埃及人掌握了人工孵化（incubation）技术，代替了母鸡亲自孵蛋，让母鸡被解放出来去下更多的蛋。

干扰 你可能不认识“incubation”这个词，但通过前面的“人工（artificial）”和后面的“解放母鸡（freed hens）”也能精准锁定这是一种不用母鸡的方法。

句子 It was in that era that Egyptians mastered the technique of artificial incubation, which freed hens to lay more eggs.

Q11

解析 除了保持温度，湿度（humidity）也必须保持在55%的稳定状态，对应了题目的条件“stay the same”。

干扰 你如果只看到上一句的温度就停下了，就会漏掉紧接着的下一句里同样要求保持稳定的另一个并列条件“湿度”。

句子 Most chicken eggs will hatch in three weeks, but only if the temperature remains at around 38 degrees Celsius. The eggs must also be turned three to five times a day, and the humidity must remain stable at about 55 percent, otherwise physical deformities can result, or the eggs won't hatch.

Q12

解析 埃及人建造的大型房间本质上就是烤箱（ovens），刚好对应了题干中“起到……作用（functioned as）”的表述。

干扰 你可能想填走廊（corridors）或通风口（vents），但仔细看句子主干，大房间的核心本质是烤箱，走廊和通风口只是连接物。

句子 The Egyptians constructed vast complexes of large rooms, which were essentially ovens, and these were connected to a series of corridors and vents that allowed attendants to regulate the heat from fires.

Q13

解析 鸡被养在室内，可以保护它们免受寒冷、大雨以及捕食者（predators）的伤害。

干扰 原文提到的恶劣温度和大雨已经属于题干中恶劣天气（bad weather）的范畴，你只需要填“as well as”后面剩下的危险来源“捕食者”即可。

句子 This allowed chickens to be raised indoors and be protected from cold temperatures and heavy rain as well as predators.
